name: ratified decisions (ADR index)
description: Single data layer = Drizzle over Neon Postgres + pgvector; matching via embeddings, dims pinned to Voyage voyage-3.5 = 1024. Open ADR-0004 / ADR-0010 before changing schema strategy or embedding dims.

name: Discovery ANN read: one deep query, wrappers never re-query
description: packages/db/src/queries/discovery.ts owns the ONLY ANN read over creator profiles. searchCreatorProfiles holds every correctness rule (status='ready', assertEmbeddingDims before SQL, conjunctive jsonb @> tags, similarity floor, similarity DESC + id ASC total order, keyset pagination, per-viewer follow state). findSimilarProfiles is a thin wrapper mapping its rows, NOT a second query — so the ADR-0018 live-smoke gate and product discovery exercise one implementation. Rule for future work: add an argument, never a parallel query. Two structural details worth copying: (a) fetch limit+1 so nextCursor is non-null IFF more rows follow rather than merely 'iff the page was full' — an exactly-full final page is the test that catches the naive version; (b) GROUP BY creator_profiles.id with max(similarity) so one row per creator is structural, not an accident of there being one embedding model, which forces threshold/cursor predicates into HAVING.

packages/db/src/queries/profiles.ts findSimilarProfiles filtered only on embeddings.source_type, never on creator_profiles.status, so unpublished draft profiles leaked into every discovery read — a live correctness bug, not a missing feature. It was invisible because a draft looks like any other ranked hit. Related silent-failure class in the same query: pgvector does NOT error on a wrong-width vector, it matches nothing, so a dimension mismatch is indistinguishable from 'no results' (ADR-0010). A third, latent one: the embeddings unique index is (source_type, source_id, model), so a creator embedded under a second model joins to two rows, and two rows sharing a profile id defeat the id pagination tiebreaker — silently skipping or repeating creators across pages.
resolution: Filter status='ready' inside the query so no read path can forget it (drafts stay visible to direct getCreatorProfileById/ByUserId lookups — the owner must see their own draft). Call core's assertEmbeddingDims() before touching SQL so a width mismatch throws EmbeddingDimensionError. GROUP BY creator_profiles.id with max(similarity) so one row per creator is structural. Each fix is pinned by a test PROVEN to fail against the old query first — that proof is the point, not the test count.

title: follows edges are user-to-user, and follow mutation stays off DiscoveryPort
rationale: The edge is (follower_id, following_id) over Better Auth user ids, not user-to-profile, because a creator profile is a REGENERABLE projection of a user (createCreatorProfile upserts on user_id) — hanging follows off the profile uuid would make the graph fragile to regeneration, and following is a member-to-member capability the moment the community slice grows, so this shape needs no migration then. The composite PK is the row's whole identity: it makes followCreator idempotent via onConflictDoNothing (a double-clicked Follow button is a UI accident, not a conflict) and indexes the 'does A follow B' direction for free; follows_following_idx serves the reverse. Self-follows throw ResonanceError('follow_self') rather than hitting a CHECK constraint, because the web layer needs a branchable typed error, not an opaque driver one. Follow MUTATION deliberately does not sit on core's DiscoveryPort — it is not ranking, and putting it there would force every alternative ranker (resonance-7890) to reimplement it.

description: An authenticated /discover search 500s on the dev Neon DB with NeonDbError 42P01 relation "follows" does not exist, while the anonymous search is fine — so the bug looks like an auth problem and is not. searchCreatorProfiles only emits its correlated 'exists (select 1 from follows ...)' sub-select when viewerId is non-null; the viewer-null branch emits the literal 'unknown' and never names the table. A committed, merged migration is therefore invisible until someone signs in. Root cause: packages/db/drizzle/0003_green_ultimo.sql shipped in resonance-663d but drizzle.__drizzle_migrations on the dev database had only 3 of 4 rows.
resolution: Check the DATABASE the code will actually run against, not just the migrations folder: select table_name from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public', and compare drizzle.__drizzle_migrations row count against packages/db/drizzle/*.sql. Apply with 'pnpm --dir packages/db db:migrate' (needs DATABASE_URL in the environment; drizzle.config.ts reads process.env, and apps/web/.env.local is the only place it lives locally). Filed as resonance-7912.

description: Reaching for a DB transaction to make a multi-row or multi-table write atomic in @resonance/db does not work: the two drivers behind 'type Db' support disjoint mechanisms. drizzle's neon-http session throws 'No transactions support in neon-http driver' on db.transaction(), and the PGlite harness used in tests has no db.batch(). So neither db.transaction() nor db.batch() compiles to working code on both, and a helper that uses either passes in tests and fails in production (or vice versa).
resolution: Make the write ONE Postgres statement — every single statement runs in its own implicit transaction, which is the only atomicity mechanism both drivers share. A batch insert is one multi-row INSERT. A multi-table write puts the extra tables in data-modifying WITH clauses via db.execute(sql`with x as (${insert.getSQL()}) ${mainInsert.getSQL()}`); drizzle insert builders are SQLWrapper so .getSQL() composes them without executing. Postgres runs a WITH clause exactly once and to completion, and child-row foreign keys resolve because RI triggers fire after the statement finishes. Pick the always-non-empty insert as the main statement, since a WITH clause inserting zero rows cannot be written. See packages/db/src/queries/observations.ts.

name: Ports that must not default a value take only the deps they need
description: createObservationAdapter({ db }) enforces core's ObservationPort invariant 'never substitute a current OS release' structurally rather than by discipline: the deps object contains no release, so there is nothing the adapter could fall back to. The column is NOT NULL with no DB default for the same reason, and a small assertAttributable guard rejects a blank string that NOT NULL would accept. Compare createDiscoveryAdapter({ db, embed }), which injects what it does need. The general rule: when a port forbids an adapter from inventing a value, the cheapest enforcement is to give the adapter no source for it — a missing dependency cannot be misused, whereas a present one relies on every future edit remembering the rule.

title: Weave pattern-registry records: jsonb metric maps, enums only where the source enumerates
rationale: The Pattern Registry's ten evidence counts and nine classification scores are stored as two jsonb columns on weave_patterns, not nineteen integer columns. The metric NAMES belong to the registry rulebook, which ADR-0020 §4 places as corpus YAML in @resonance/weave-os; a column per metric would make the db schema a second copy of that list that can silently diverge, and adding a metric would cost a migration instead of a corpus edit. PatternEvidenceMetricsSchema and PatternClassificationScoresSchema type them at the boundary, matching how creator_profiles types its jsonb offerings. The registry holds tens of rows, so no index is justified on those maps — over-indexing a tiny table is the real mistake. Relatedly: lifecycle status (7) and promotion target (4) are TS unions because the source document enumerates them outright, while promotion_readiness, promotion_decision, discovered_during and current_scope_hypothesis have exactly one attested value each and no declared set, so they are carried as plain text rather than a guessed enum. Architect/Validator fields are absent because those entities are out of scope per ADR-0020.

title: embeddings.source_id is text, not uuid — the vector store is polymorphic in ID SHAPE
rationale: The embeddings table keys a vector to its source row, but sources do not share an id type: a creator profile is a uuid, a member's interest vector is keyed to their Better Auth user id, which is text. A uuid column can hold one of those and not the other, so the wider identifier type wins (migration 0005, ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE text — Postgres accepts this without a USING clause via I/O conversion, preserves uuids in canonical lower-case form, and rebuilds the unique index automatically, so no hand-edit of generated SQL was needed). Two consequences: comparisons are now EXACT TEXT comparisons, so a uuid-shaped source id must be stored canonical (every current writer passes an id straight back from the database, so this holds); and searchCreatorProfiles joins with creator_profiles.id::text = embeddings.source_id. THE CAST DIRECTION IS LOAD-BEARING: source_id::uuid would raise 'invalid input syntax for type uuid' the moment the planner evaluated it against a non-uuid source id such as an interest row, and nothing in SQL guarantees the source_type filter is applied first. Casting the uuid side is always safe and the ANN scan dominates the query cost anyway. Blast radius checked and clear: verify-live.mjs untouched (its eq() binds a string), findSimilarProfiles' frozen signature unchanged; apps/web/e2e/lib/discovery-fixtures.ts needed its ::uuid cast dropped.

name: Two-statement atomicity: a data-modifying WITH whose DELETE and INSERT touch disjoint rows
description: A 'replace this set' write (setMemberInterests) cannot use a transaction — Neon's HTTP driver has no interactive transactions and PGlite has no batch, the constraint queries/observations.ts documents. The naive delete-all-then-insert-all is NOT safe to collapse into one statement: data-modifying CTEs all see the same snapshot, so the INSERT's uniqueness check still sees the rows the DELETE is removing, and ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING then silently drops a re-selected row. The fix is to make the two halves touch DISJOINT rows: scope the DELETE to rows NOT in the new set (notInArray) and let the INSERT's ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING absorb the rows that survive. Then 'with removed as (<delete>) <insert>' is a single atomic statement with no row affected twice. The same trick works for the derived vector: the WITH clause prunes interest rows under a DIFFERENT model while the upsert owns the row for the current one — which is what makes 'a member has exactly one interest vector' true by construction, so the read never has to arbitrate between two models. Compose with drizzle builders + .getSQL() + db.execute(sql`...`), exactly as insertEvaluation does.

content: Hand-written SQL migrations go through 'drizzle-kit generate --custom --name <name>', never a hand-added journal entry. The custom flag prepares the empty .sql file AND registers both the _journal.json entry and the meta/NNNN_snapshot.json, so the next db:generate still diffs from the right baseline; hand-editing the journal leaves a gap where the snapshot should be. This is the sanctioned path for the two things drizzle-kit cannot generate: Postgres extensions (0000_enable_pgvector) and curated reference DATA (0006_seed_topics — the 13 topic rows the interest picker renders). Seed data belongs in a migration rather than a dev script when the feature is broken without it: pnpm db:migrate is the one step every environment already runs, and createTestDb() applies every real migration, so tests then exercise the same taxonomy production has and a broken seed fails a test instead of passing silently. Use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING so the seed is seed-once, not enforce-forever — the point of a taxonomy table is that it can be edited as data afterwards.

description: A committed migration that is not applied to the dev Neon DB breaks the running app the moment the code lands, and the fast gate cannot see it — the exact shape of mx-a981bb (Slice A shipped the follows table to main, left dev unmigrated, and every AUTHENTICATED /discover search 500'd for six steps while anonymous search kept working). Slice B repeated the setup: dev was still at 0003 (already one behind 0004 Weave OS, which is deferred) with embeddings.source_id as uuid, so the new join creator_profiles.id::text = embeddings.source_id would have failed there with 'operator does not exist: text = uuid'. Migrations are the one artifact where a green unit suite proves nothing about the database the code will actually run against.
resolution: Before finishing any schema seed, query the dev DB directly rather than trusting the drizzle folder: read drizzle.__drizzle_migrations, information_schema.columns for the columns you changed, and a row count. Then run db:migrate (drizzle.config.ts reads DATABASE_URL from process.env; there is no packages/db/.env, so export it from apps/web/.env.local) and VERIFY the outcome, not just the exit code — for this change: source_id is text, all 63 embedding rows preserved, all 63 still join to a profile through the new cast, indexes intact, 13 topics seeded, 7 migrations applied. Note that catching up also applies any intervening migration (0004's dormant Weave OS tables here), which is correct: verify-live's migrations check already treats the committed journal as the truth dev must match.

name: Personalized ranking is another source for the query vector, not a second query
description: DiscoveryPort invariant 8 ('no query text ⇒ rank by the viewer's stored interests') was implemented WITHOUT touching searchCreatorProfiles, which stays the one ANN read. createDiscoveryAdapter resolves the query vector from one of two sources — embed(query.text), or getMemberInterestEmbedding(db, viewer.userId) — and both flow into the identical ranking call, so invariants 2-7 (ordering, threshold, limit, draft exclusion, follow state, keyset paging) hold on the personalized branch for free rather than being restated. The empty-page fallback (no viewer, or no stored vector) is checked BEFORE the embedder is reached, which is what keeps the absent text — a literal JS undefined — from ever being handed to it; every adapter test in that block injects an embedder that throws for ANY text, so reaching it fails the test. A typed query always wins over stored interests — it is the more current signal — so the two branches stay separate rather than collapsing into one nullable vector. The interest WRITE ships as a direct db export, not a port method, following the precedent DiscoveryPort already sets for follow mutation ('it is not ranking'). Return a FRESH empty page object per call, not a shared const: the page is handed to callers and a shared literal lets one caller's mutation leak into the next.

mx-3c75df's rule 'do NOT auto-apply migrations to close a dev-DB gap' targets UNATTENDED application, whose danger is specific: drizzle-kit renders a column rename as DROP COLUMN + ADD COLUMN, which is silent data loss. That danger is READABLE IN THE GENERATED SQL, so the rule can be applied by inspection rather than as a blanket ban. Slice B's 0005 contained CREATE TABLE, ADD CONSTRAINT, CREATE INDEX and one ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE text — no DROP, no rename — and 0006 was an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Not applying was ALSO not free here: the branch's new join (creator_profiles.id::text = embeddings.source_id) fails outright against a uuid column, so shipping the code with dev unmigrated reproduces mx-3c75df exactly.
resolution: Read the generated SQL before deciding, and treat DROP COLUMN / rename as the actual trigger for handoff-instead-of-apply. When you do apply: snapshot the dev DB first (drizzle.__drizzle_migrations, information_schema.columns for the touched columns, a row count), apply, then PROVE the data survived rather than trusting the exit code — for 0005 that was source_id is text, 63/63 embedding rows preserved, 63/63 still joining to a profile through the new cast, indexes intact. Report the application explicitly in the handoff either way, because it is a mutation of shared infrastructure the diff does not show. DATABASE_URL is not in packages/db/.env; export it from apps/web/.env.local for drizzle.config.ts.

description: A UI-only PR (packages/ui + design docs, zero db/e2e files) went red on discovery E2E with 'NeonDbError: operator does not exist: text = uuid'. Cause is cross-seed, not the branch: E2E runs against a SHARED, PERSISTENT Neon DB (secrets.DATABASE_URL) and CI does NOT run migrations. The parallel Slice B db seed (resonance-e2d0, branch feat/slice-b-db, commit 2f9457a) widened embeddings.source_id from uuid to text in migration 0005 and APPLIED it to that shared database, while its matching code fix stayed on its own unmerged branch. From that moment every branch cut from main failed Slice A's discovery E2E, because main still casts `source_id = ${id}::uuid`. Migrating a shared DB from a feature branch silently breaks every other branch until that branch merges.
resolution: Compare both sides as text so the SQL is agnostic to which state the column is in: the fixture drops the ::uuid cast entirely (`source_id = ${id}`, letting the column drive the bound parameter type), and the discovery join becomes sql`${creatorProfiles.id}::text = ${embeddings.sourceId}::text`. Verified against BOTH shapes — 62 db unit tests pass against PGlite where source_id is still uuid, and the Neon e2e passes where it is text. Prefer this double-cast over the one-sided cast on the db branch, which only works once the migration is authoritative. Structural fix worth considering: have CI run migrations, or give E2E an ephemeral branch DB, so a shared mutable schema stops coupling unrelated branches.
